summary: Self-service access requests stall when Okta 'department' attribute contains semicolon-delimited values
description: Issue summary: Self-service access request flows in the internal support portal are entering a stuck state (request shows 'Pending, awaiting approver' indefinitely) for a subset of employees. Impact: Affected engineers cannot gain time-sensitive access to Model Observability dashboards and runbooks; several oncall actions were delayed ~45–90 minutes during triage on 2026-03-10. Environment: production (us-west) auth flow backed by Okta + SCIM provisioning into RBAC service. Observed symptom: requests are created but not assigned to an approver queue; support-portal logs show assignment step skipped. IDP logs show user group assignment present, but RBAC service receives department attribute as a single semicolon-delimited string and fails role-map lookup.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) User with Okta profile where department="Platform;Data" attempts self-service request for 'modelobservability' role in support-portal.
2) Support-portal POST /access-requests succeeds and request record created (request_id in logs).
3) Background assignment job calls rbac-service /map-role using SCIM-provisioner user payload.
4) rbac-service returns 204 but with no approver assigned (assignment metadata missing).
5) Request remains in 'Pending' with no approver or escalation triggered.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 15:00 — Aisha: Reproduced locally by crafting SCIM payload with department containing semicolon; observed map function expects array or single token separated by comma. Hypothesis: recent IdP attribute normalization change started emitting semicolon-delimited department lists for users with multiple affiliations.

2026-03-10 16:10 — Marcus: Confirmed Okta change — expression in profile now concatenates multiple departments with ';' after last Okta update. SCIM provisioner forwards attribute as-is. Our rbac-service parsing logic only splits on ',' and whitespace, so 'Platform;Data' is treated as a single unknown key.

2026-03-11 09:20 — SRE: Observed ~12% of recent access-requests in last 24h had department containing ';' and 100% of those were unassigned. Related incident impact correlated with peak oncall activity window.

root_cause_summary: Okta started emitting multi-valued 'department' attribute with semicolon separators after a profile-expression change. The SCIM provisioner forwarded the attribute verbatim and the RBAC role-mapping logic only parsed comma-separated values, causing a mismatch that left assignment metadata empty and requests unassigned.
resolution_summary: Temporary workaround: support manually approved stuck requests and identity team applied an Okta profile-transform expression for affected groups to emit a single canonical department value for critical users. Deployed short-term scim-provisioner patch in production to normalize ';' to ',' and added immediate backfill job to re-run assignment for requests created since 2026-03-09T00:00:00Z. Long-term fix: rbac-service to implement multi-delimiter parsing and a validation check that raises an alert when assignment metadata is missing.

2026-03-11 13:10 — Canary deploy to prod for 10% of tenants; monitored assignment success for 30m (no failures).

2026-03-12 — Follow-up: rbac-service parsing ticket opened and scheduled for next sprint; add alert rule for unassigned access requests.

Run an IdP attribute normalization audit for all multi-valued fields and update Confluence runbook with canonical formats.
resolution: In Progress (workarounds applied; short-term patch deployed; longer-term changes scheduled)
notes_for_csr_handling: If customer/internal user reports stalled request: (1) check request history for assigned_assignee field, (2) if null, escalate to identity-eng channel and perform manual approval for P1s, (3) record affected user department value and tag ticket with 'dept-separator' for backfill.
